title: Above-Band Offer Approval Based on Misidentified Precedent
question: Should the Nakamura offer at $275K base + 12,000 RSUs be approved as proposed, citing the Reeves precedent?

contributor.name: Jasmine Torres
contributor.title: Senior Total Rewards Analyst
contributor.domain_expertise: Compensation band management, equity refresh cycles, job leveling frameworks, offer approvals

choices: Yes — the Reeves exception establishes precedent for above-band L6 offers when candidates have competing offers at higher comp.

No — the Reeves exception was a board-level one-time acqui-hire approval explicitly marked as non-precedent-setting; the base exceeds the current band ceiling and requires a new exception request through proper channels.
No — the offer cannot proceed because VP Eng declined the comp committee meeting, and VP-level approval is required for any above-band offer.
Yes — the $275K base is within market range per Pave data (75th pctile = $272K) and only $7K above band ceiling, making it a de minimis exception the hiring manager can approve.
